learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will correctly apply coordinating, subordinating, and correlative conjunctions to link ideas, build compound/complex sentences, and ensure smooth transitions.]
warm_up_hook: 🌉 If words are bricks, conjunctions are the cement holding them together! Without them, our writing would be short, choppy, and robotic. Today, we are putting on our hard hats and learning how to build bridges between our ideas! 👷‍♂️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Coordinating conjunctions connect two equal independent clauses or equal grammatical items. Remember the acronym FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So.
examples_or_templates: Connecting Nouns: I like apples AND oranges.
Connecting Clauses: It was raining, SO we stayed indoors.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These conjunctions introduce a dependent clause, making it rely on an independent clause for meaning. They show relationships of time (until, when), cause/effect (because, since), or condition (if, unless).
examples_or_templates: Cause/Effect: I went to bed early BECAUSE I was exhausted.
Condition: UNLESS you study, you will not pass the exam.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These are tag-team conjunctions that always travel in pairs to join equal elements. Common pairs include Either/Or, Neither/Nor, Both/And, and Not only/But also.
examples_or_templates: Pair 1: EITHER we leave now, OR we miss the train.
Pair 2: She is NOT ONLY smart BUT ALSO incredibly hard-working.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which FANBOYS conjunction best completes the sentence: 'She was very tired, _____ she continued to work on her project.'
❓ Identify the correlative conjunctions in the sentence: 'He is both a talented musician and a skilled athlete.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Combine these two sentences using a subordinating conjunction: 'The match was canceled. It rained heavily.'
subjective_practice.hint: Try using a word that shows cause, like 'because', 'since', or 'as'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blanks with the correct correlative conjunction pair: '_____ my brother _____ my sister likes broccoli; they both hate it.'
subjective_practice.hint: Since they both hate it, use the negative pair.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🧱 The Bridge Builder
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write a 5-sentence story about a hero facing a monster. Your challenge: You must use at least one FANBOYS conjunction, one Subordinating conjunction (like 'although' or 'because'), and one pair of Correlative conjunctions (like 'not only/but also'). Highlight them!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS) connect equal parts of a sentence.
⭐ Subordinating conjunctions connect dependent clauses to independent clauses to show time, reason, or condition.
⭐ Correlative conjunctions work in pairs (Either/Or, Both/And) to balance sentence elements.
